proposals: The Tamil Nadu government should publish the draft Prohibition and Excise amendments and retail licensing rules for public comment before tabling, including any cap on the number of licences one entity may hold, so the safeguards against a repeat of the 2001–03 auction cartels can be examined in advance.

Tamil Nadu's Prohibition and Excise Department should allocate private retail licences through an online lottery with published applicant lists and results, the kind of auditable allocation Uttar Pradesh uses, given that the TASMAC allegations concern opaque tendering.

Tamil Nadu's Finance Department should publish an estimate of the revenue effect of privatising 2,500 shops — expected licence-fee receipts against the retail income given up, since the government has itself acknowledged a possible shortfall it would need to cover.

Tamil Nadu's Prohibition and Excise Department should publish quarterly, by district, MRP-overcharging complaints, inspections and licence suspensions for private shops, so whether private licensing actually disciplines overcharging can be checked after the change.

The RBI's annual study of state finances should report each state's liquor revenue split into excise duty, VAT and licence fees on a common definition, so comparisons like Tamil Nadu's ₹48,344 crore against Uttar Pradesh's ₹52,573 crore no longer mix different definitions.
